description: We’ll write a story about a particular topic
summary:
I created Cosmic Explorer, an interactive web game where players pilot a rocket across space between Earth, the Moon, and Mars. While managing a depleting oxygen meter and gathering refills, players navigate using radar to discover and scan 14 real-world NASA milestones, including the Apollo 11 lander, the Curiosity rover, the ISS, and the Webb Telescope.

Space science and history often feel abstract or boring when taught only through static textbooks. The game solves this challenge by turning real space missions into an active cosmic scavenger hunt. Crucially, each discovery rewards points and unlocks a practical, offline challenge—such as folding a paper helicopter like Ingenuity, testing laser reflections with a flashlight, or tracking the ISS overhead.

This project is important because it bridges digital gaming with tangible, real-world learning. Instead of promoting passive screen time, it sparks genuine interest in STEM, celebrates human exploration, and motivates players to observe, build, and experiment in everyday life.
details:
1. What It Does & How It Works

  • Flight & Navigation: Players pilot a rocket across a 2D space map (Earth, the Moon, and Mars) using an edge radar and minimap to track down 14 real NASA milestones (e.g., Apollo 11, Curiosity, James Webb).
  • Survival & Scanning: Players manage a depleting oxygen meter by gathering canisters or refueling near Earth and the ISS. Approaching a target lets players scan it to reveal historical facts and unlock a real-world task.
  • Dual Rewards: Accepting real-world tasks grants bonus points and oxygen refills, with progress saved automatically via local storage.

2. Benefits

  • Active Learning: Replaces dry textbook reading with interactive space exploration.
  • Offline Engagement: Directly connects gameplay with real-life, hands-on activities (e.g., folding paper helicopters, stargazing, flashlight experiments).
  • Instant Accessibility: Runs immediately in any browser with zero downloads, logins, or ads.

3. Intended Impact

  • Spark STEM Curiosity: Inspires students and young learners to take an interest in space exploration, science, and engineering.
  • Promote Healthy Screen Time: Uses digital achievements to motivate physical creativity and offline experimentation at home or in class.

4. Tools & Technologies Used

  • Languages: HTML5, CSS3, and Vanilla JavaScript (ES6+).
    • HTML5 Canvas 2D: Procedural rendering of planets, atmospheres, orbits, and particle trails.
    • Web Audio API: Real-time synthesized sound effects and background tones without audio files.
    • Pointer & Touch Events: Unified controls supporting desktop keyboards and mobile virtual joysticks.
    • LocalStorage: Seamless client-side progress saving.
  • Hardware: Any modern device (PC, tablet, smartphone, or Chromebook).

5. Creativity

  • Digital-to-Physical Game Loop: In-game discoveries reward players for committing to hands-on, offline experiments.
  • 100% Asset-Free Engine: The entire visual universe, particle effects, and soundscape are procedurally generated through code rather than pre-baked image/audio files.

6. Factors Considered

  • Accessibility: Responsive UI with auto-scaling and seamless controls for both touchscreens and keyboards.
  • Player Experience: A directional radar prevents players from getting lost, and running out of oxygen triggers a gentle tow back to Earth rather than a frustrating penalty.
  • Child Safety & Privacy: 100% client-side operation with zero data tracking, sign-ups, or third-party dependencies.
